newsitem.title: UK: Yorkshire-Tyne H1 ad revenues below budget.
newsitem.headline: Yorkshire-Tyne H1 ad revenues below budget.

text.p: Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings Plc reported sharply higher first-half profits on Tuesday but said advertising revenue in the first six months was "well short of budget."

Yorkshire-Tyne Tees, one of the regional ITV television companies, reported first-half pretax profits rose to 13.3 million stg from 7.4 million a year-ago. Turnover increased to 136.1 million stg from 129.7 million last year.
"This successful result has been achieved despite the fact that advertising sales performance has been very disappointing," chairman and chief executive Ward Thomas said in a statement.

"The smaller than expected increase in total ITV advertising revenues compounded the lack of growth in our net advertising revenue share," Thomas said. "As a result our half-year advertising revenue is well short of budget and we are exerting pressure on Laser, our sales agency, to deliver to the level called for under our contract with them."
An increasing success on the programme side and cost controls more than compensated for the advertising sales shortfall, he said.
First half advertising revenues rose to 84.6 million stg from 81.8 million in the 1995 first half.

Sales of programmes in the UK grew to 38.2 million stg from 36.3 million, and overseas programme sales edged up to 3.16 million from 3.12 million. Other income climbed to 10.1 million stg from 8.5 million.

Thomas said the company continues to look at digital television. "We, and others we consider well informed, believe that it will be some considerble time before there is a substantial digital audience and indeed there is doubt as to whether there will ever be a large audience for an expanded terrestrial service of this kind," he said.
